payload.feature: Judge, without implementing or shipping, the branch fire/0047-supersede at commit 80f36b0, one commit on top of main 0b10649, delivered by run decision-0047-docs-decisions-004-522a821e whose verify gate passed and whose review gate could not run (the codex account's usage limit is exhausted; the run was concluded on that reason). The commission that commit answers is decision 0047 (docs/decisions/0047-the-finding-is-closed-by-name.md, accepted 2026-09-06): the `brokkr operator supersede` verb on a terminal run, appending one `operator/commanded` event with `command: "supersede"` and args `{ findings: [seq...], by: { realm, run_id, seq }, reason }`, no acceptance following; cite-or-say-nothing verification at write time (terminal status, each finding seq a residual finding the view derives, `by` resolving to a transition/decided in the named journal, not self); the fold unchanged and byte-identical with the annotation appended; `ResidualFinding.superseded` on every surface that prints a residual finding; the dossier carrying the mark, the annotation as a citable fact, and a `superseded_findings` count; the Muninn charter leaving superseded findings out of the queue and stating how many; the `contracts/operator-supersede.v1.schema.json` payload schema under the additive rule with the v1 envelope, the `type` enum and every witness digest unmoved; the guides. Read the decision, then the commit, then the tests, and judge whether each of the six rulings' enforcement bindings is actually enforced, whether any refusal path fails open, whether a test constructs a shape the real CLI or compiler cannot produce, and whether anything beyond the decision was changed. The exact coverage gate, clippy -D warnings, fmt, and cargo test --workspace are the verify seat's; your judgment is the rest. Write the result file with the typed inputs; put findings in notes, most severe first, each with a file and line.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

result.notes: This seat asserts nothing: it is a placeholder ahead of the protected review gate. Verification for this judgment is the pull requests own checks.

Reviewed fire/0047-supersede at 80f36b0 (one commit on main 0b10649) read-only against decision 0047: the decision, the whole diff, and every test. All six rulings are enforced; no refusal path fails open; no frozen material was edited (contracts/ gained one additive file with its witness row in frozen_contracts.rs; policy/, reference/, fixtures/ untouched; the muninn charter has no digest pin anywhere — library_data.rs lists it under AUTHORED_CHARTERS without a sha and no bundle names it); nothing beyond the decision changed in substance. Four low findings and two info notes remain, none security.

FINDINGS, most severe first:

1. low · correctness (ruling 4) · crates/brokkr-cli/src/muninn.rs:260-267. The 'covered' filter compares the annotation's by.realm with the dossier's source key. The verb validates --by-realm as ONE realm name (lib.rs supersede(), the hearth.realms.iter().any(...) match) and records that name; Muninn keys a many-hearth source by Hearth::label(), which joins the realms sharing a journal with '+' (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/realms.rs:124). For a hearth serving two realms the key is 'a+b' while the mark says 'a', so the superseding run's ruling is never admitted as a citable fact even though the reading covers that journal. Fails closed (a report citing it is refused as 'does not state'), hence low. The two-hearth CLI test (tests.rs the_supersede_verb_records_one_annotation_and_refuses_the_rest) uses one realm per journal and never meets the case.

2. low · correctness (ruling 2 / contract) · crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs supersede(), `None => invocation.journal.clone()`. With --by-realm omitted the citation is verified against invocation.journal, which is --db when --db is given, and the annotation records realm: null. The contract (contracts/operator-supersede.v1.schema.json by.realm) and ruling 2 define null as 'the workspace journal'. In a mapped world where --db names a realm's own journal, the recorded citation misnames where the cited run lives: a reader following null to the workspace journal finds nothing, and the dossier's covered check (finding 1) never matches it. Verification itself still happens before the write, so this is a record-precision gap, not a fail-open.

3. low · test-coverage (ruling 5) · crates/brokkr-cli/src/muninn/tests.rs a_report_may_cite_the_annotation_and_leaves_the_finding_out_of_the_queue. The 'queue omits the finding' assertion inspects a work_queue the test itself wrote without seq 6; nothing in validate() (muninn.rs:485-495) refuses a work_queue entry citing a superseded finding's ruling seq, which remains a stated fact. The only enforcement of 'a superseded finding is not queued' is charter prose — which is what the decision's binding names, so the code is per decision — but the test proves less than its name says. A validator refusal would be a one-line hardening beyond the decision as written.

4. low · fit (decision 0001 consistency) · crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs listed_run() (~1100-1114), hearth_runs() (~1655), and the single-hearth Runs arm (~2436). Residuals are now derived from a journal even when the fold refuses it, so a quarantined row in runs --json, ui and the tui model carries derived findings and marks, while the dossier (muninn.rs:157-188) substitutes a quarantine finding and derives nothing from that journal. Two read surfaces answer differently about a quarantined run.

5. info · Cmd::Operator.db moved from a defaulted arg to Option<PathBuf>; retry/stop behaviour is preserved by unwrap_or(DEFAULT_DB) (lib.rs run_with Operator arm) but --help no longer shows the default. RunRow.residuals reaches every fleet model (tui RunsView, ui JSON), not only runs --json — a consequence of one model, acceptable.

6. info · security: none. --by-realm is checked against the map's realm names and --by-run/--by-seq against the cited journal (opened read-only, chain-verified by Store::load) before the fenced append_next_if_head; the fold arm at core/fold.rs:219 is untouched; reason and the cited id reach inspect through Safe (render.rs inspect) and the trail through the clamped Safe at render.rs:545. The other two writers of operator/commanded (engine.rs:2465, 2994) always write args: {}, so a 'supersede' command word arriving via the bridge or the retry/stop path yields no mark (view supersede_of requires /args/by and /args/findings).

CONFIRMED ENFORCED: R1 verb + schema + fold byte-identity test (fold/tests.rs a_supersede_annotation_folds_a_stopped_run_to_the_same_state, engine test validates written args against the published schema). R2 all five refusals precede the first append and each has a test (engine/tests.rs a_supersede_whose_citation_does_not_resolve_writes_nothing; CLI-level refusals in tests.rs); head fence tested with a peer append; read-time rule tested by concluding the superseding run afterwards. R3 RunState gains nothing; ResidualFinding.superseded on the model, the line, the header ruling (last decision), the trail row and runs --json; last annotation wins; VIEW_VERSION 9. R4 mark, annotation fact, count, and the cover check (with finding 1). R5 charter rule 5 + fleet_summary clause; a 'supersede' proposal is refused because terminal runs admit no command. R6 phase machine untouched; status asserted unchanged. Tests extend the suites that prove the code; test shapes are ones the store and engine produce (append_next-built journals), the view tests' synthetic envelopes are fine for a pure derivation.
